question: At matched quality, does native ternary inference (BitNet b1.58 2B4T) substantially outperform strong optimized INT4 on this CPU?
scope_limits: single x86 laptop CPU under WSL2; not an ARM/Jetson/edge target
no energy measured (Stage 2 needs separate approval)
quality via log-likelihood multiple-choice subsets; absolute scores differ from the model card

QWEN25_1P5B_Q4KM.why: highest card average of the comparison set: the closest quality match to BitNet

QWEN25_1P5B_Q40.why: same model in the simplest 4-bit block format (no k-quant overhead)

QWEN25_3B_Q4KM.why: stronger, larger comparator (not in the BitNet card); re-added after review because the 1.5B-class models alone could leave no INT4 model at or above BitNet's quality. First attempt from the Qwen repo was too slow, the bartowski mirror is used

LLAMA32_1B_Q4KM.why: smaller, lower-quality comparator, same tokenizer family as BitNet

SMOLLM2_1P7B_Q4KM.why: mid-quality comparator with a different architecture

quality.note: tasks include MMLU (500) added after review; 4 tasks became 5
quality.macro: unweighted mean of the four task accuracies

performance.perf_set_rule: quality is measured first; timing runs only for BitNet and INT4 models with quality macro >= BitNet macro - 5.0 (written to results/ternary_vs_int4/perf_models.json by `summarize select` before any timing)
performance.power_rule: every timed invocation records AC/charge; the harness refuses to time on battery or below the minimum charge
performance.thread_rule: per (model, runtime, regime short: prompt<=1024 / long: prompt>=2048): the thread count with the lowest median end-to-end latency at that regime's sweep cell, fixed before the main run

decision_rule.comparator: per metric per cell, the fastest INT4 (model, runtime) in the matched pool = INT4 models with quality macro >= BitNet macro - tolerance (conservative for ternary)
decision_rule.empty_pool: if the pool is empty the outcome is NO_MATCHED_COMPARATOR: no ratios are computed (no fallback to weaker models); a quality-vs-speed table of all timed models is reported instead
decision_rule.headline: geometric mean over the 8 grid cells of the end-to-end latency ratio (INT4 time / ternary time)
flags: AUDIT_DECODE_EXCEEDS_BANDWIDTH_IMPLIED_RATIO (decode geomean > geomean of per-cell (INT4 bytes streamed per token incl. KV) / (ternary bytes) x 1.2; bytes from GGUF tensor types, see bytes_model.py)
COMPARATOR_ABOVE_TOLERANCE_TERNARY_DISADVANTAGED (a chosen comparator's macro quality exceeds BitNet's by more than the tolerance: the comparison is not matched)
decision_rule.interpretation: Speed/memory only. Not an energy result, not evidence about FlexTern hardware. The 2.0/1.3 energy thresholds in the founder directive apply to Stage 2.

preregistered_prediction.basis: static GGUF tensor accounting before any timing (bytes_model.py)
preregistered_prediction.statement: BitNet 2B4T streams more bytes per decoded token than Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_K_M because its tied 128k-vocabulary embedding/head is stored in F16 (about 0.66 GB of its 1.18 GB) and its KV cache per token is larger (5 KV heads x 30 layers vs 2 x 28). So a bandwidth-bound decode should NOT be faster for BitNet than for that comparator; a decode speed-up above the bandwidth-implied ratio would indicate a compute-side effect of the I2_S kernels. HYPOTHESIZED, to be checked by the measurements.

pre_lock_disclosures: protocol was revised after an independent pre-lock review and before any measurement: Qwen2.5-3B re-added, MMLU added, empty-pool fallback removed, bytes-ceiling audit replaced by tensor-level accounting, per-regime thread sweep, explicit flash-attn, power refusal rule, shorter foreground budget

before the lock I ran load-only smoke checks and two 1-repetition llama-bench smoke runs (BitNet tg8 about 14.5 tok/s; a 64-token-prompt/16-token run showing BitNet about 14.9 vs Qwen2.5-1.5B Q4_K_M about 17.8-18.7 tok/s decode). They were used only to validate the harness and are not data; the preregistered prediction below was derived from static GGUF accounting, but it was written after those smoke numbers were visible, so it is not blind
missing_by_design: TL2 kernel for the ternary model was not built (ternary side uses I2_S only: it may be under-optimized)
no OpenVINO run (BitNet is not supported there; INT4-only comparison would not test the question on this AMD CPU)
